name: Jarque–Bera normality diagnostic
variables: n sample size; m_j empirical central moments; g_1 skewness; g_2 non-excess kurtosis
assumptions: Independent observations, nonzero sample variance, sufficiently large sample for the asymptotic chi-square(2) reference under normality.
limitations: Tests selected moment departures; non-rejection does not demonstrate normality. Small-sample asymptotics can be inaccurate.
failure_conditions: Zero variance or unmodelled serial dependence
computation: Calculate centered moments and JB statistic; apply the large-sample null reference only when justified.

source.citation: SciPy maintainers, jarque_bera API and references. https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.jarque_bera.html

application: Diagnose distributional assumptions of comparable residual measurements on authorised development data.
required_inputs: Large authorised independent sample of comparable real-valued measurements.
incompatible_methods: Using dependent residuals as independent without adjustment

name: Wald–Wolfowitz binary runs diagnostic
definition: For n_1,n_2 counts of two binary symbols, n=n_1+n_2, let R=1+Σ_(i=2)^n 1(s_i≠s_(i−1)), μ_R=1+2n_1n_2/n, σ_R²=2n_1n_2(2n_1n_2−n)/(n²(n−1)); Z=(R−μ_R)/σ_R.
variables: Ordered binary sequence s; n_1,n_2 symbol counts; R run count; μ_R and σ_R² conditional null moments
assumptions: Null exchangeability of the ordering conditional on counts; both symbols observed, positive null variance, prespecified binary encoding.
limitations: Normal approximation requires sufficient counts; use an exact conditional reference for small samples. Detects only some departures from randomness.
failure_conditions: No variation, post hoc binary threshold, or an unjustified ordering null
computation: Count symbol transitions and calculate conditional moments; use exact or justified asymptotic reference.

source.citation: NIST Engineering Statistics Handbook, Runs Test for Detecting Non-randomness. https://www.itl.nist.gov/div898/handbook/eda/section3/eda35d.htm

application: Assess order dependence in a prespecified binary encoding of historical residual measurements.
required_inputs: Authorised ordered binary development sequence with a documented encoding and tie policy.
incompatible_methods: Sorting the sequence by observed value before assessing chronological randomness

name: Exact paired mean sign-flip permutation test
definition: For n paired differences d_i, T=Σ_i d_i/n. Under independent uniform sign flips conditional on magnitudes, p=2^(−n)Σ_(s∈{−1,+1}^n)1(|Σ_i s_i d_i/n|≥|T|).
variables: n matched pairs; d_i difference; s sign vector; T mean difference; p two-sided exact tail probability
assumptions: Joint null invariance under independent sign reversals (for example independent symmetric differences); correct matching and prespecified two-sided statistic.
limitations: Exponential enumeration cost; does not test a zero mean under arbitrary asymmetric or dependent distributions.
failure_conditions: Lack of sign-exchangeability or incorrect event matching
computation: Enumerate sign patterns for small n; for larger n a separately specified randomization approximation requires reproducible seeds and uncertainty reporting.

source.citation: SciPy maintainers, permutation_test API, permutation_type='samples' for a single paired-difference sample. https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.permutation_test.html

application: Compare matched development measurements while retaining magnitudes under a justified sign-exchangeable null.
required_inputs: Authorised matched differences with a defensible randomization or symmetry assumption.
incompatible_methods: Unjustified independent sign flips of clustered or serial differences
mechanism_note: Uses magnitudes in the test statistic rather than merely counting positive signs.
